chunks: Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ‘Ali ibn Shajarah, from Salām Al-Ju’fi, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad Al-San’āni, from Abū Ja’far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) would draw Ḥusain (peace be upon him) to himself whenever Ḥusain (peace be upon him) would enter. Then he would tell the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) to hold him, after which he would fall on him, kissing him and crying. So (Ḥusain) asked, 'O father! Why are you crying?' He replied, 'O my son! I am kissing the place of the swords from you.' (Ḥusain) said, 'O father! And I will be killed?' He replied, 'Yes, by Allāh, and your father and your brother and you.' (Ḥusain) said, 'O father! Then our places of martyrdom will be far apart.' He replied, 'Yes, O my son.' (Ḥusain) said, 'So who from your nation will come to our Ziyārah?' He replied, 'No one but the truthful ones from my nation will come to my Ziyārah, to the Ziyārah of your father, to the Ziyārah of your brother, or to your Ziyārah.'

key_terms.مَوْضِعَ السُّيُوفِ: Place of the swords (referring to martyrdom)

ai.seo_question: Who will perform Ziyārah to the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Kamil al-Ziyarat highlights the Prophet’s prophetic foresight by kissing the 'place of swords' on Ḥusain’s body, a motif central to Shia devotion emphasizing the inevitability of Karbala. It further establishes a spiritual hierarchy where only the al-Ṣiddīqūn (the truthful) can truly visit the collective presence of the Prophet, Ali, Hasan, and Husain, linking physical pilgrimage to spiritual fidelity.
